You are the implementer. 
GOAL: a "sentry" (сторож) for user astrahancev-maxim-911aird on a shared Linux hub (~150-200 users, 32 cores, 122 GB RAM, NO swap, no GPU).
All of this user's AI agents, builds, tests and browsers run inside ONE systemd cgroup (the T3 service):
  T3CG = /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/system-t3\x2dserver.slice/t3-server@claude\x2dastrahancev\x2dmaxim\x2d911aird.service
  (literal backslash-x2d in the directory name; discover it robustly: glob /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/system-t3*server.slice/t3-server@*astrahancev*maxim*911aird.service, allow override via env SENTRY_CGROUP).
  Measured 05.11: cpu.max "800000 100000" (8 CPUs, kernel-enforced), memory.max 52755525632 (49 GiB), memory.high max, pids.max 4096, NO io.max (disk IO unlimited), memory.stat has anon/file/inactive_file.
  Inside it: T3 server (node /usr/bin/t3 serve ..., oom_score_adj -900), agent CLIs (claude under … codex, antigravity, node acp bridges; oom_score_adj 800), and heavy jobs.
The sentry will be started by cron every minute with flock -n (so it runs in /system.slice/cron.service, NOT inside T3CG — never use /proc/self/cgroup to find T3CG). It must be a long-lived loop (sample every 5 s), exit by itself after ~24 h so cron restarts fresh code, and use negligible CPU/RAM.

Why: on 02.11 the hub ran out of RAM (our bots + headless browsers), on 04.11 our pids hit 4096 (T3 could not start agents) and a 6-thread download wrote 93 GB and slowed the hub disk. The owner just removed self-throttling (no agent-count limits, no hub-loadavg gate), so this sentry is the safety net. It must act ONLY at critical levels and ONLY on our heavy processes.

WRITE: multicode/tools/scripts/hub-sentry.py (Python 3 stdlib only, run as python3 -I, no pip) and multicode/tools/scripts/hub-sentry.md (short Russian doc: what, thresholds, files, how to switch off, cron line). Touch NO other files.

PROCESS UNIVERSE: only PIDs listed in T3CG/cgroup.procs (and cgroup.procs of any sub-cgroups under T3CG), owned by our uid. Never signal anything else.

KILLABLE ALLOWLIST (everything else is NEVER killed, only reported):
  - chrome: exe basename in {chrome, google-chrome, chromium, chromium-browser, chrome-headless-shell} or exe under /opt/google/chrome/; a "browser root" = such a process WITHOUT a "--type=" argument. EXCLUDE any chrome whose exe path is under the user's ~/.t3/ (that is T3's own preview browser, managed by T3).
  - godot: exe basename starts with "godot" or "Godot" (case-insensitive), e.g. .../tools/godot/4.7.2/..., .../polus/.hub-tools/godot/...
  - unity_player: exe under a path containing "/duckpit/build/" (e.g. DuckPit.x86_64).
  - unity_editor: exe path containing "/tools/unity/editors/" (Unity batchmode builds) — lowest priority, killed only for memory/pids criticals and only if nothing else qualifies.
  - downloader: exe basename in {curl, wget, aria2c, rclone, yt-dlp} — only for the disk-IO rule.
  Killing a job = SIGTERM to its root process (the allowlisted process whose parent is NOT an allowlisted process of the same kind), wait 5 s, then SIGKILL the root and every remaining descendant. Before every signal re-check that the PID still has the same starttime (field 22 of /proc/PID/stat) to avoid PID reuse. NEVER signal: the T3 server, any agent CLI (claude/codex/antigravity/node/bash/sh/python that is not itself allowlisted), cron, sshd, mutagen, the sentry itself or its ancestors.

RULES (each threshold env-overridable, defaults below; a condition must hold for 2 consecutive samples before acting; after a kill wait 20 s before the next kill for the same rule):
  R1 hub RAM: /proc/meminfo MemAvailable < SENTRY_HUB_MIN_GB=8 GB  -> kill the NEWEST allowlisted job (by root start time) whose tree RSS >= 300 MB; unity_editor last.
  R2 our RAM: (T3CG memory.current - inactive_file) > memory.max - SENTRY_OWN_RESERVE_GB(=5) GB -> same selection as R1.
  R3 our pids: T3CG pids.current > pids.max - SENTRY_PIDS_RESERVE(=500) -> kill the NEWEST allowlisted job whose tree has >= 50 threads (count threads from /proc/PID/status Threads).
  R4 Chrome count: browser roots (as defined, excluding ~/.t3) > SENTRY_MAX_CHROME=2 for >= 30 s -> kill the newest extra roots, keep the 2 oldest.
  R5 orphan Chrome: a browser root with ppid == 1 and age > SENTRY_ORPHAN_MIN=45 min -> kill it.
  R6 disk writes: sum over our processes of delta write_bytes (/proc/PID/io; skip unreadable) -> 60 s average > SENTRY_IO_WARN_MBS=150 MB/s => notify only; 180 s average > SENTRY_IO_KILL_MBS=250 MB/s => kill the top writer (by its own delta over the window) ONLY if it is allowlisted (incl. downloader); otherwise notify only.
  CPU and the hub loadavg are NEVER a reason to act (CPU is kernel-capped at 8 cores); log them only.

FILES: state dir multicode/.cache/hub-sentry/ (create it): log (one line per action/notify, plus a heartbeat status line every 10 min; if > 5 MB keep the last 1 MB), state.json (last notify time etc.).
  Switches: if multicode/.cache/hub-sentry/off exists -> do nothing (log "off" at most once per hour); if multicode/.cache/hub-sentry/dry exists or --dry-run -> log what it WOULD kill, kill nothing.
NOTIFY: Telegram via multicode/tools/tgbot/send.sh "text" (text is the FIRST argument; call with a 30 s timeout, never block the loop on failure), at most one message per 10 min (aggregate the rest into the next one), Russian, first line = verdict, e.g. "Сторож хаба: убил Chrome PID 123 (2.1 ГБ, сирота 50 мин). У хаба свободно 7 ГБ, у нас 31/49 ГБ, потоков 900/4096."
CLI: --status (one sample: numbers, Chrome roots, allowlisted jobs, what it would do now; exit 0), --once (one evaluation pass then exit), --dry-run, --selftest.
SELFTEST (mandatory): the decision logic must be a pure function over an injected snapshot (no /proc access​), and --selftest must assert at least: R1..R6 each trigger with the right victim; must-NOT-kill cases (a 20 GB claude agent, the t3 server, a codex process, T3's ~/.t3 chrome-headless-shell, bash/python agent shells, a non-allowlisted heavy writer) are never chosen; 2-consecutive-sample hysteresis; newest-first selection; unity_editor last; Chrome count keeps the 2 oldest; dry-run kills nothing; PID-reuse guard (starttime mismatch => no signal). Exit 0 only if all pass.

Then RUN (all safe, kill nothing): python3 -I multicode/tools/scripts/hub-sentry.py --selftest ; python3 -I multicode/tools/scripts/hub-sentry.py --status ; python3 -I multicode/tools/scripts/hub-sentry.py --once --dry-run . Fix until selftest passes and status/dry-run run without errors on the real machine.
MUST NOT: install any cron, start the loop in the background, send real Telegram messages (in dry-run/status/selftest do not call send.sh; or point SENTRY_NOTIFY_CMD to a no-op), kill or signal any process, touch files other than the two named and the .cache/hub-sentry/ dir.
Return: what you wrote (thresholds, allowlist), the full selftest output (counts), the --status output, and anything you could not verify.
